finding.claim: Broken authorization: wipe() calls requireRole(), which only returns a boolean and never throws, and discards the result. Any authenticated user can wipe any tenant, regardless of role. The sibling export() correctly uses the throwing checkRole().
finding.source: POST /tenants/{t}/wipe: an authenticated low-privilege user (without the OWNER role) supplies the tenant path parameter.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27, a destructive wipe of tenant data.

trace.note: requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role); the doc comment says it does not throw
return value of requireRole(u, "OWNER") is discarded, so the check has no effect
sibling export() uses checkRole, which throws SecurityException, so it is SAFE

finding.guards_checked: Role check at line 26 is not enforced because the result is unused and the function never throws. There is no other auth, ownership or tenant-scoping check in wipe(). The export() handler's checkRole is enforced (it throws), so export is SAFE with respect to the role check.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole at src/Admin.java:14 returns a boolean and never throws, and wipe() discards the result at line 26. No other auth, ownership or tenant-scoping check exists in wipe(). I did not search the rest of the directory for callers or a wrapping filter.
verdict.reason: src/Admin.java:26 calls requireRole (defined at :14, returns boolean and never throws) as a bare statement, so repo.wipe(tenant) at :27 runs for any authenticated user, whereas export() at :32 uses the throwing checkRole (:18-21).
